patients.summary: Young man with bilateral cataract surgery at 20 who joins in 2020, is diagnosed with myotonic dystrophy type 1 by neurology in 2023, Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) with azoospermia by genetics in 2024, and AV conduction disease by cardiology in 2025. By 2026 he has dysphagia, weight loss and confirmed low testosterone, and is weighing fertility options before any testosterone.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 22 y/o man who moved into an apartment in town this summer and has not had a regular doctor since his pediatric office. Membership explained, agreement emailed. Intake booked for 9/22 at 9:00. He will sign a release so we can pull his old office records and the eye surgery records from 2018.

conditions.label: Presence of intraocular lens
conditions.note: Bilateral cataract extraction with IOL, 2018, age 20

documents.title: New Patient Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22 y/o M here to establish. Last regular care was his pediatric practice in high school. Feels well. No complaints today.

PMH: none ongoing. Cataracts in both eyes found at 20; had them taken out with lens implants, right then left, summer 2018 at an outside surgery center. Vision fine with glasses for reading now and then. Says he had some trouble with reading in school, thinks it was mild dyslexia, never formally treated.
PSH: bilateral cataract extraction w/ IOL (2018).
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father has a muscle disease, pt not sure what it is called, and also had cataracts young. Mother healthy. Nothing known on mom's side.
SHx: works part time on the sales floor at a store in town. Lives on his own, has a girlfriend. Never smoked, does not drink, no drugs. Right-handed.

ROS: negative in full except as above.

Exam: tall, thin young man, NAD. HEENT: pupils round and reactive, IOLs in place, TMs clear, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rash. Strength and gait grossly normal.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: screening HIV and hep C, CBC, CMP, lipids. Flu vaccine given. PHQ-2 negative. Will get childhood shot records and Tdap date from old office.
2. History of bilateral cataract surgery at 20, pseudophakic. Eye follow-up with his surgeon as they advise.
3. Family history of a muscle disease in father: asked him to find out the name from his dad.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Zachary, all of your blood work from Tuesday is normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were both negative. Nothing to do. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Prior pediatric office and eye surgery records
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received by fax, 31 pages.

Pediatric office (care through 2016): routine well visits, normal growth with a fast height gain in the teen years. Childhood immunization series complete. Tdap 08/11/2015. No chronic conditions listed.

Outside eye surgery center: bilateral visually significant cataracts in a 20 y/o. Right eye phacoemulsification with posterior chamber IOL 07/10/2018, left eye 08/07/2018. Both uncomplicated. Post-op visits with good acuity in each eye.

Abstracted into chart. Scanned to media. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: COVID vaccine card
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got both of my covid shots at the pharmacy (April 13 and May 4). Uploading a picture of the card so you have it.

documents.title: Physical and flu shot
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got the reminder for my yearly physical. Work is crazy through the holidays, can I push it to after New Year's? Also going to skip the flu shot this year if that's ok.

documents.title: RE: Physical and flu shot
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No problem. You are booked for Tuesday 2/8 at 8:30. Doctor says the flu shot is still recommended, and you can stop in for one anytime if you change your mind.

reports.text: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 64. PR 168 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 408 ms. Normal axis. No ST or T wave abnormality. No prior tracing for comparison.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Doing fine, still part time at the store, picking up extra shifts. No new problems. Eyes good since surgery. Two COVID doses last spring. Skipped flu this season.

Asked again about his father's diagnosis; he still does not know the name, only that it is a muscle problem that started in his dad's 30s. Pt has no symptoms of his own. Given the family history and no prior tracing, got a baseline ECG today.

Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker, no EtOH.
Exam: well appearing, tall and lean. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd benign. Strength full, gait normal.
ECG: NSR 64, PR 168, QRS 92, normal.

A/P: Healthy 23 y/o. Baseline ECG normal, filed for comparison. CBC/BMP. PHQ-2 0. Encourage flu next fall. Return in a year.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your ECG and blood tests from yesterday all look normal. We'll keep the ECG on file to compare against in the future.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after work for flu and the bivalent COVID booster. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Flu in L deltoid, COVID in R deltoid. Waited 15 min without issue. VIS given.
